items.t: 젠슨 황이 '겁먹은 사슴'이라 비하한 임원, 엔비디아 새 수장으로… 콜레트 크레스는 누구?
items.d: 젠슨 황 전 엔비디아 최고경영자(CEO)가 과거 공개적으로 깎아내렸던 임원이 자신의 후임으로 회사를 이끌게 됐다. 황 전 CEO가 불륜 의혹으로 사임하면서 엔비디아의 임시 CEO에 오른 콜레트 크레스 최고재무책임자(CFO)가 그 주인공이다. 12일(현지시간) 월스트리트저널(WSJ)과 AP통신 등에 따르면 황 전 CEO는 지난 8월 고위 재무 담당 임원들과의 회의에서 크레스 CFO를 향해 “헤드라이트 앞에 선 사슴 같다”고 비판했다. 갑작스러운
items.fullText: 국제 젠슨 황이 '겁먹은 사슴'이라 비하한 임원, 엔비디아 새 수장으로… 콜레트 크레스는 누구? 발행일 : 2026-11-14 14:30 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) X(트위터) --> 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 콜레트 크레스 엔비디아 임시 CEO. 사진=로이터 연합뉴스 / 엔비디아 젠슨 황 전 엔비디아 최고경영자(CEO)가 과거 공개적으로 깎아내렸던 임원이 자신의 후임으로 회사를 이끌게 됐다. 황 전 CEO가 불륜 의혹으로 사임하면서 엔비디아의 임시 CEO에 오른 콜레트 크레스 최고재무책임자(CFO)가 그 주인공이다. 12일(현지시간) 월스트리트저널(WSJ)과 AP통신 등에 따르면 황 전 CEO는 지난 8월 고위 재무 담당 임원들과의 회의에서 크레스 CFO를 향해 “헤드라이트 앞에 선 사슴 같다”고 비판했다. 갑작스러운 상황에 당황해 제대로 대응하지 못하는 사람을 뜻하는 표현이다. 당시 황 전 CEO는 엔비디아가 추진하던 대규모 금융 지원 계약의 위험성을 점검하기 위해 회의를 소집했다. 엔비디아는 자사 반도체 구매 여력이 부족한 클라우드 업체 등에 수십억달러 규모의 신용 보증을 제공하는 방안을 추진하고 있었다. 이 과정에서 황 전 CEO의 사위인 니코 카프레즈 부사장도 거래를 주도했다. 엔비디아는 고객사의 자금 조달을 지원하는 대신 매출 일부를 공유받는 구조를 구상했다. 그러나 크레스 CFO는 지원 대상 선정 기준과 보증 가치 산정, 투자수익률 계산 방식 등에 의문을 제기하며 거래 확대를 견제했다. 특히 지난 1월 부사장으로 승진한 카프레즈의 움직임을 제어하려 했던 것으로 전해졌다. 황 전 CEO는 회의에서 크레스를 전략 수립이나 의사결정에 도움을 주는 인물이 아닌 단순히 재무 수치를 보고하는 CFO라고 평가했다. 당시 엔비디아는 주요 클라우드 업체들이 자체 반도체와 대체 제품으로 눈을 돌리는 가운데, 이미 구매를 약속한 반도체 웨이퍼와 메모리 물량이 부담으로 작용하는 상황이었다. 황 전 CEO는 이를 '눈사태'에 비유하며 위기감을 드러냈다. 크레스 CFO는 실제로 엔비디아의 금융 지원 규모를 축소하는 데 관여했다. 엔비디아는 오픈AI가 사용할 오하이오주 초대형 데이터센터 건설 사업에 최대 2500억달러의 금융 보증을 검토했지만, 크레스는 초기 지원 약정 규모를 절반으로 줄였다. 양사는 지난 8월 17일 축소된 조건으로 계약을 체결했다. 이후 엔비디아는 일부 클라우드 업체에 대한 신규 금융 지원 계약을 보류하고 심사 절차를 강화했다. 2013년 엔비디아에 합류한 크레스는 마이크로소프트와 시스코, 텍사스인스트루먼트 등에서 재무 업무를 담당한 베테랑 경영자다. 엔비디아가 AI 반도체 시장을 장악하는 과정에서 투자자들과 소통하고 주요 금융 거래를 설계하는 역할을 맡았다. 그는 황 전 CEO의 갑작스러운 사임으로 지난 12일 임시 CEO에 선임됐다. 황 전 CEO는 중국 정보기관과 연계된 것으로 의심받는 여성 및 엔비디아 직원과의 부적절한 관계가 보도된 뒤 자리에서 물러났다. 다만 중국 외교부는 관련 첩보 의혹을 부인했다. 크레스는 취임 후 직원들에게 보낸 메시지에서 “지난 33년간 젠슨이 구축한 놀라운 토대 위에서 회사를 계속 발전시키겠다”고 밝혔다. 엔비디아는 현재 황 전 CEO와 관련한 내부 및 연방 차원의 조사를 받는 동시에 AI 투자 확대에 따른 재무 위험에 직면해 있다. 주가도 지난 10월 사상 최고치 대비 30% 이상 하락했다. 엔비디아 이사회는 내부와 외부 인사를 모두 대상으로 차기 정식 CEO 후보를 검토할 예정이다. 시장에서는 크레스의 경영 능력을 높이 평가하면서도 외부 인사가 최종 후임자로 낙점될 가능성을 배제하지 않고 있다. 서희원 기자 shw@etnews.com

Colette Kress Will Face Scrutiny at Nvidia
items.d: Nina Trentmann, senior editor at Bloomberg News, says Colette Kress is likely to become more visible as Nvidia’s interim CEO, speaking more about the company’s finances, performance and plans after Jensen Huang’s departure. She speaks with Vonnie Quinn on “The Close”. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.t: Jensen Huang’s departure blasts big hole in AI startup funding, VCs and founders say
items.d: Nvidia poured tens of billions into AI startups under Huang. Without him at the helm, founders and VCs are bracing for smaller checks and lower valuations.
items.fullText: It was the resignation heard across the world. Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s embattled CEO who co-founded and led the company for 33 years, had officially stepped down . “It’s like a bomb went off,” one neocloud founder told TechCrunch when he first heard the news. Over the last several years, Nvidia has been a prolific investor , pouring tens of billions into startups annually and participating in 105 rounds this year alone, often as the largest investor, according to PitchBook. “If that direction changes, it’ll be a big blow to so many young companies,” said Maria Davidson, founder of Relational Capital. Huang’s absence leaves the startup ecosystem without one of its biggest champions and with far less capital for now, investors say, which could have a massive impact on dealmaking, valuations, funding, and even competition. “Nvidia is carrying almost every AI-native startup from application to neocloud,” Dawn Capital’s Shamillah Bankiya told TechCrunch. Most of the significant decisions to invest in startups often came from Jensen himself, according to Umesh Padval, managing partner at Seligman Ventures. Padval has known Huang since serving on the board of Mellanox Technologies, a networking chipmaker Nvidia acquired for approximately $7 billion in 2020. While there is hope that Huang’s eventual successor will resume his dealmaking spree, investors aren’t hopeful that it will happen in the short term. Nvidia’s interim CEO, Colette Kress, is expected to institute some changes , especially when it comes to Nvidia’s investments into AI startups at the crux of the billion-dollar data center build-out . items.t: Export-banned Nvidia chips are behind China’s most powerful AI models — uh-oh, Jensen!
items.d: New research shows the most advanced AI models from China were trained on banned Nvidia chips.
items.fullText: The leading open-weight models developed by Chinese companies were trained on Nvidia chips that the U.S. government restricted from shipping to its largest geopolitical rival, a new research effort claims. The apparently widespread access to Blackwell GPUs among Chinese frontier labs shows the magnitude of the problem facing the leading chip designer. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang left the company this week after admitting to his affair with Alice Huang, executive of Megaspeed, a company implicated in smuggling Nvidia chips into China. Alice Huang has also been alleged to be an agent of China’s intelligence service. While Jensen Huang’s relationships with a customer and two employees have drawn the most public interest, Nvidia’s potential corporate liability for export control violations likely factored into its decision to part ways with Huang. U.S. export controls are intended to protect the country’s leadership in AI capabilities against China, but Huang has long sought to open up that market. Blackwell GPUs are banned from export to China or Chinese-owned firms, while the Trump administration allows Nvidia to export the H200, a less powerful chip, provided shipments take a circuitous shipping route that allows the U.S. to claim a 25% tariff. Will DePue, a former OpenAI researcher who leads the nonprofit research group Unemployment Labs, analyzed the weights — the unique structure — of large language models released openly by DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group. The weights still reflect the configurations of the chips used to train them, and DePue was able to find compelling evidence that the most closely watched models, including Moonshot’s Kimi’s K3 releases and DeepSeek’s V4 models, bear fingerprints from training on Blackwell chips. items.t: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
items.d: Jensen Huang has resigned from Nvidia following an affair, which could have ramifications for national security as the U.S. and China race to develop the most advanced AI infrastructure.
items.fullText: Nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as prone to controversy as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. But the 63-year-old industry kingpin recently admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security. U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.) Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported. The story took a sudden turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up. By early Thursday morning, Huang was no longer CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another extramarital affair with another unnamed Nvidia employee. The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. items.t: Israel’s VCs see opportunity for challengers in Nvidia’s turmoil
items.d: Given Nvidia’s stronghold on AI and its importance in Israel, many in the country's startup ecosystem are worried about the impact of his departure.
items.fullText: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation has been received with worry in Israel, the company’s “second home,” as Huang described it in 2023. The company’s importance flows both ways, as the semiconductor giant has provided a major boost to Israel’s economic forecasts in recent years. Intel, Microsoft, and many homegrown startups also conduct a sizable share of their R&D in Israel. But owing to Nvidia’s stronghold on AI given the centrality of its GPUs for training LLMs and using them, many in the country are wondering how much of a reshuffle will result from the company’s leadership crisis. As with everything at Nvidia, Huang drove the company to acquire Israeli chipmaker Mellanox for $6.9 billion in 2019 and use the company as the base for its largest R&D facility outside of the U.S. Nvidia also made plans to build a multibillion-dollar campus in northern Israel. “Jensen brought Nvidia to Israel with the acquisition of Mellanox, so there is a strong positive sentiment towards Nvidia and Jensen in Israel’s tech community,” Israeli repeat cybersecurity entrepreneur Pavel Gurvich told TechCrunch. Beyond the 6,000 locals Nvidia employs, the bigger question is whether the company will remain as committed to Israel with someone else at the helm. As a result, his line of succession is being observed just as closely by those who hope the company continues to do so as by those who don’t want it to happen. The latter have already gathered that they may be in for disappointment. In a 2023 interview that is now doing the rounds on X, interim CEO Colette Kress had declared that as Nvidia’s CFO, she typically started her day “with Israel meetings, and only then continue[d] to California.” Kress may not remain in charge in the long run, but the many names floated for the role include two Israelis , Apple’s Johny Srouji and Nvidia’s Michael Kagan — although they’re not at the top of the still quite tentative list . items.t: Jensen Huang didn’t show confidence in his successor, report says
items.d: Huang described Kress as a "deer in the headlights" during a meeting in summer.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 4:28 AM PST · November 13, 2026 Image Credits: Nvidia (opens in a new window) Ivan Mehta Jensen Huang didn’t show confidence in his successor, report says Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang described Colette Kress, the company’s CFO who has now replaced him as interim CEO, as “a deer in the headlights” during a presentation earlier in the summer, the Wall Street Journal reported , citing an anonymous source. Huang made the comment during a meeting with Nvidia’s finance team about the company’s plans to provide guarantees worth billions of dollars to data center operators that couldn’t afford to buy its chips up front, according to the report. He reportedly also said Kress was a person who couldn’t help him steer strategy or decision-making. Kress has been with Nvidia for over 13 years now , after serving as SVP and CFO of Cisco’s Business Technology and Operations Finance. The report said she has questioned Nvidia’s program-focused, credit-based deals involving Huang’s son-in-law Nico Caprez, and wanted to know how to decide which deals are beneficial, how to value guarantees, and determine returns. Earlier in the year, she had scaled back on Nvidia’s commitment for OpenAI’s ambitious Ohio data center project. The company was in talks to provide $250 billion in credit to OpenAI but ended up committing $105 billion . Huang resigned Thursday after reports of two extramarital affairs , including one with the company’s VP for healthcare, Kimberly Powell. The company is also investigating a possible Chinese espionage plot . After Huang’s resignation, Reuters reported that he was having a third affair with another employee . Nvidia is currently searching for a permanent CEO to replace Huang, who had the top job for over 33 years. items.t: Democrats launch Nvidia investigation, write scathing letter on Huang’s ‘scheme’ with Trump
items.d: This Congressional investigation into Nvidia's China sales and its dealings with Trump is the second one, so far, since news of the alleged spy affair broke.
items.fullText: Democrats on Thursday opened an inquiry into how the Trump administration handled Nvidia’s chip sales to China. Earlier on Thursday, the company ousted its CEO Jensen Huang . He also agreed to testify to a different set of Republican-led Congressional committees. Huang was removed from the company he founded after he confessed to an extramarital affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. (He has since been accused of having more affairs , with Nvidia employees.) The alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, was an executive of Nvidia customer Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that U.S. officials suspect of helping route advanced Nvidia chips into China. The Democratic inquiry comes from Rep. Richard Neal (D-Mass.), the top Democrat on the House Ways and Means Committee, and Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), the top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee. As the minority party, they can ask questions but can’t compel answers. Their humdinger of a letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick asks the department to preserve records about an arrangement they find questionable and, they allege, illegal. “The scheme worked like this,” as the letter describes it. President Trump agreed to sales of Nvidia’s H200 chips to China as long as the chips, manufactured by Taiwan, were first shipped to the United States. On arriving, Trump added a tariff “effectively taking a cut of Nvidia’s sales to China through what appears to be an unconstitutional export tax system,” the letter said. Then the Commerce Department, under Lutnick, issued an export license. By the way, the deal between Trump and Nvidia to share revenue was public. In August 2025, Nvidia and AMD both agreed to share 15% of their revenue from chip sales to China with the U.S. government as part of a deal to secure export licenses, the AP reported at the time.
